appearance_facts.location: right edge of plot, x≈2030, y≈955
appearance_facts.fact: May bar is a very short dark red rectangle whose top sits just above the x-axis baseline, far below the 10,000 gridline.
Apr bar is a tall dark red rectangle reaching just under the 30,000 gridline.
Jan bar is the tallest dark red rectangle, reaching the 40,000 gridline.
Jun bar is a medium dark red rectangle reaching just above the 15,000 gridline.
Feb bar is a medium dark red rectangle reaching the 20,000 gridline.
Mar bar is a tall dark red rectangle reaching just above the 25,000 gridline.

printed_facts.fact: X-axis category labels left to right: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May.
May bar height corresponds to a value well below the lowest labeled tick (10,000 m3), the minimum among all six months.
Reference highs: Jan ≈ 40,000 m3; Apr ≈ 29,500 m3; Mar ≈ 27,000 m3.
Reference mid values: Jun ≈ 17,500 m3; Feb ≈ 20,000 m3.

public_definitions: Options: 'Route May to standard low-release follow-up', 'Escalate May to critical low-release anomaly review', 'Send May to background monthly record filing'.
uncertain: No explicit numeric value label is printed on the May bar; its magnitude is read only from bar height relative to the 10,000 m3 tick.
No threshold, band, or reference line on the chart defines the boundary between 'standard low-release' and 'critical low-release anomaly', so the severity cutoff is not stated in the chart.
